recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Restoring the original FHIR-14138 wording would contradict later Published decisions; future changes should be made through the resolve-as-version-specific issue family.
issue_request: FHIR-14138 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I STU3 change request asking the HTTP transaction rules to clarify that a client could use an arbitrary versionId in a version-specific reference to a resource whose server-assigned version was not yet known, because the server would update the reference during transaction processing.
initial_application: HL7/fhir commit 39bbdfc466f00e43e561a63ae7a34104d306feed applied the issue by adding the sentence that clients could use arbitrarily chosen version references because they would be re-assigned. FHIR-14005 was resolved No Change because this issue was considered to answer the same transaction-reference ambiguity.
additional_context: The linked 2017 Zulip thread shows both the original local-version-id assumption and early concern about unintentionally rewriting references to older historical versions. FHIR-34344 later explicitly said the FHIR-14138 text was not careful enough, removed the arbitrary-version/re-assigned wording, and approved replacement text distinguishing existing version-specific references from references to versions created in the current transaction. FHIR-34343 approved the resolve-as-version-specific extension for the latter case; later cleanup and example issues retained that mechanism.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/http.html already contains the later Version specific references and updates section, the superseded arbitrary-version text is absent, the Extension Pack defines resolve-as-version-specific, and source/bundle/bundle-transaction.xml demonstrates the extension for server-assigned ids and versions.

related_jiras.note: Asked the same version-specific transaction-reference question and was resolved No Change because FHIR-14138 answered it.
Later Published issue explicitly removed the broad FHIR-14138 arbitrary-version wording and replaced it with the current transaction guidance.
Approved the resolve-as-version-specific extension that supplies the current mechanism for transaction-created or transaction-updated target versions.
Cleaned up link and duplicate-text errors in the same replacement narrative.
Added a transaction Bundle example demonstrating resolve-as-version-specific for Provenance targets.
